must_fix: Beats 7-9 credit the wrong cause for the fix. Beat 7 says 'one new rule' and beat 8 says 'it says so', implying that saying 'can't see' fixed the count. FACTS: the count went from 14 to 11 because of three filters (joints below 0.4 confidence thrown out, knee angles under 30° thrown out, reps must last 0.8 s), not because of a 'say so' message. Rewrite as plural rules, e.g. 'So I taught my AI to throw out what it can't see.' Put the three limits on the diagram, and keep 'can't see? say so' as the guardrail tag.

Beat 8's 'If it can't see my knee, it says so' and the HUD line "can't see your knee on rep [N]" present a judge behaviour as working. FACTS say the judge is still being built and none of its outputs are measured. reps_clean.json records thrown-out frames (34 hidden, 24 impossible), not a per-rep message. Either show the line only once the HUD or judge really emits it, or mark it [SLOT: guardrail message]. Also confirm that some rep actually has a hidden knee before slotting [N]; 34 frames may not make up a whole rep.

Beat 6 / K9 tie both fake readings to 'The machine hid my leg'. Only the 11° knee came from occlusion. The 0.2 s 'rep' (115° torso lean) came from the tracker jumping between joints, and the half reps at the clip start and end (reps 1 and 14) are part of the 14. Rewrite the tags so the 0.2 s tag says 'tracker jumped joints', or reword the speech, e.g. 'The machine hid my leg, and my AI guessed anyway.' Do not imply that occlusion explains all three extra reps.

Beat 3's 'My AI would have stopped me' is an unmeasured verdict spoken as fact. It is true only if the judge returns STOP on [BAD_SET]. Mark it [VERDICT]-dependent the same way as the beat-1 stamp, and add it to the 'not recordable' list.

The TRIAL hook 'My AI said it was fine' rests on the form-labeller (reference coach, confidence 0.6). Neither the analyser nor the judge has a measured verdict on IMG_2649. The on-screen equation 'MY AI = WORKOUT ANALYSER' would then misattribute it. Either slot the analyser's verdict on IMG_2649 or label the source on screen as 'AI coach' (labeller). The caption's 'Good set... it said so' has the same problem and should say the coach/labeller verdict.

CTA 'Comment FORM to run this on your own sets' overclaims. The form-labeller skill grades frame sheets; it is not the analyser pipeline (pose, knee wave, best-set baseline, judge). Promise only what ships on posting day, e.g. 'Comment FORM to get the full diagram and my form-check skill', and match the caption and first comment to it. This also fits the creator's 'name the benefit' CTA voice.

Beat 12 says 'not the topper's' while the screen and the locked section title say 'not a textbook', with a textbook crossed out. Pick one image: either keep 'topper' in speech and draw a 'topper' doodle, or say 'not a textbook' and keep the Indian comparison elsewhere. Brief section 7 is titled 'MY BEST, NOT A TEXTBOOK'.

Beat 12 says 'compares every rep' in the present tense, but the judge is not built or measured. Make sure the baseline comparison really runs before recording, or keep the line as a design statement backed by the diagram's 'being built'-safe wording.

Beat 10's 'So always let your AI say "I can't see"' is vague for non-builders. A clearer everyday action: 'So always ask your AI to tell you what it can't see.' This keeps the creator's verbatim-able 'So always...' shape.
Beat 1 runs 0-3.9 s at 1.0x, against the brief's 0-3 s; the stamp lands at about 3.6 s. Tighten to land the stamp by 3 s, e.g. 'My AI found the set I should never have done.' (10 words).

The runtime section quotes 1.15x; the house rule and the brief target 1.1x. At 1.1x the estimate is about 48 s with 1.5 s of holds, the top of the 42-48 s window, before beat 2 is filled. Pre-plan the trim: drop beat 13, as already suggested, or merge beats 9 and 10.

Beat 3 / K5 cuts from [BAD_SET clip] to IMG_2649. Cold viewers may read IMG_2649 as the bad set, and the previous reel's tease circled it STOP. The tag should say 'test clip (a good set)' or similar, so the explainer clip is not confused with the caught set.
Beat 3 on-screen text '17 joints · every frame' slightly overclaims: 3.1% of frames had no usable pose raw, and 6.6% were thrown out after the fix. Use '17 joints · 30 frames a second'.
Beat 9 'Same clip, second try' depends on beat 5 to make sense. Per the script skill (each beat recordable alone), use 'After the fix: eleven reps, same as me.'

Caption: 'Plot twist if you saw my last reel' plus a numbered verdict is good. But 'deep on every one' should read as the coach's verdict, not the analyser's (see the trial-hook fix), and '[VERDICT + one reason]' must stay a slot until measured.

personas.why: The blocked knee explains a bad reading in one shot. I'd send the 14-to-11 fix to a teammate who's had to debug a confidently wrong alert.
I like that 11 is a count I can check. Once the corrected number lands and he states the lesson, I think the reel is over.
The red gap makes me want to see what went wrong with the lift. By the blank rule card, I'm waiting for an answer about the workout, not a rule for the software.
The frozen rep gets me past three seconds. When the knee turns into a graph, it looks like I'm about to learn how to count squats rather than when to stop.
I can follow the wave and laugh at ‘fourteen; I did eleven.’ I miss the leg being hidden because I'm trying to read the angle and timing labels.
The dot turning into a wave makes this feel like a project I could actually build. I'd comment FORM for the runnable skill, not just the picture.
Same clip, different result is a tidy before-and-after. I get the value of rejecting bad inputs; the underlined takeaway is my cue to swipe.
I'm interested enough to wait for the benchmark. ‘My best set’ leaves me asking who established it was good, so I'm not invested in the judge's verdict.
I'd save the diagram to explain to a client why a system needs an ‘I can't see’ option. I stay to see what the final output actually looks like.
‘Compared to whom?’ earns my attention back. After the baseline is revealed, ‘one set did not match’ just tells me what the opening already showed.
The ghost stops my thumb and the miscount is the moment I'd replay. The big takeaway card feels like an end screen; I wouldn't wait for a second hook.
The green ghost is memorable, especially when I learn it's the same lifter. Cutting to a row of thumbnails just when I want the side-by-side takes me out.
Seeing the obstruction, the discarded readings and the changed output makes the fix tangible. I'd try the skill on a clip with a partially hidden leg.
I'd watch to see how the judge handles low-visibility reps. One corrected count is a good demo, but agreement with another model wouldn't make me share STOP as a validated call.
I want to inspect the actual rep against the ghost. I'd comment on whether the difference matters; looking different from your best rep isn't by itself a reason to stop.
The machine blocking the knee makes the joke about three extra reps click for me. Once it gets eleven, I have the story I'd tell a friend and keep scrolling.

top_fixes: Make the measured surprise the cold open: show the counter over the actual clip and say, “My AI counted 14 squats. I did 11.” Cut straight to the machine blocking the knee. That story works even if no set earns STOP.

If the bad-set hook stays, keep that rep on screen long enough to see the fault in motion. Label the hack squat as a separate counting test; a correct count on that clip is not evidence that the first lift was dangerous.

Use beat 9 as a bridge, not an ending: “Now it can count my reps. Can it tell which one changed?” Cut the takeaway card at 10 and the thumbnail tease at 13; go from the personal baseline straight to the comparison.

At the payoff, spend the screen time on two synced reps and one plain-English observation. Prefer “the set it flagged” to “the set I should never have done.” Move the pipeline and second-model agreement into the promised diagram.
Make the CTA name the thing viewers will get. Show one second of the skill running on a clip if it's ready; otherwise offer the diagram without promising a workout analyser.
